## Summary of the last run

The page is a careful development of the representability theorem. I checked the definition of Q, the numeral lemma, Σ-completeness, the class 𝒞 and its closure properties, the elimination of primitive recursion via β, the representability proof (initial functions, composition, regular minimization), the normal-form lemma, the Σ-definability/semidecidability theorem, the problems and the supplement. The proofs are correct: the minimization case properly uses (O3) and the numeral properties, the composition case correctly forces witnesses to be numerals, and the hypcheck accurately records which axioms are used. The supplement's claims about R (Tarski–Mostowski–Robinson), essential undecidability, Church's theorem, the arithmetical hierarchy, and MRDP are all standard and correctly stated. The remark on Robinson arithmetic correctly notes that the literature's version cannot prove commutativity. I found no genuine logical gap, missing hypothesis, improper link, or false stated-only claim; the only candidate I considered (the Π₂-conservativity of IΣ₁ over PRA) is in fact the standard formulation and correct, so I do not report it.
